entities.name: PMID:30988725
observations: Cristea et al. studied 27 spondyloarthritis patients (24 men) and 26 healthy controls using culture, PCR, and serology.
Urine was tested for Chlamydia trachomatis DNA using the Chlamydia trachomatis Quant Real PCR kit.
C. trachomatis DNA was not detected in urine from any patient or control: 0/27 versus 0/26.
The cohort was spondyloarthritis rather than an ankylosing-spondylitis-only cohort; the reported urine comparison did not show increased prevalence.

entities.name: Spondyloarthritis
observations: In the available comparative study, urinary C. trachomatis DNA prevalence was 0/27 patients, including 24 men, versus 0/26 healthy controls.

entities.name: Chlamydia trachomatis
observations: Urinary DNA was assessed by real-time PCR in a spondyloarthritis cohort and healthy controls; no positive urine specimens were found in either group.
